messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PoC trial plan & deployment mode - Acme Corp

Thanks again for the time today, Alex — good conversation. Per our discovery call, I wanted to recap where we landed and propose next steps for the PoC/trial so we can validate the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC).

Key notes from the call:
- Primary use case: product search ranking + summarization for the Acme support portal (high QPS during business hours).
- Initial throughput target: ~200 requests/sec peak, average ~60 rps.
- Latency goal: p99 < 300ms for generation endpoints.
- Data sensitivity: customer support transcripts (PII present) — Priya will confirm classification and whether samples can be shared for evaluation.

Deployment mode considerations we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding, good for early evaluation; may need to validate burst handling and regional residency.
- Dedicated capacity: predictable throughput, isolated pool for production SLA; recommended if steady high QPS.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): required only if Acme needs on-prem or strict data residency/isolation beyond VPC peering.

Proposed PoC/trial plan (outline):
1) Week 0 (prep): exchange sample data & success criteria, confirm stakeholders (dev, infra, security).
2) Week 1-2 (trial): sandbox endpoints — Hosted API with dedicated trial option (reserved pool) if you want to stress test production-like throughput.
3) Week 3 (evaluation): run load tests + qualitative evaluation against sample prompts; measure latency, accuracy, and cost per 1k tokens.

Success criteria (draft):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 targets met during representative load.
- Throughput: sustained 200 rps peak or clear scaling plan on dedicated pool.
- Quality: top-3 ranking accuracy >= 85% on held-out prompts.
- Security/compliance: acceptable data handling model (VPC/retention/KMS) per Acme security team.

Next steps / asks for Alex/Priya:
- Confirm whether you want us to run the PoC on Hosted API only, or include a Dedicated trial (we can provision a short-lived reserved pool).
- Share the security contact and a sample of anonymized transcripts (or a pointer to where we can pull samples).
- Confirm availability for a kickoff next week (proposed Jun 17).

I've attached a one-page PoC plan and a simple success criteria spreadsheet to make this concrete. Looping in Marissa (solutions) and Rishi (CS) to align on timeline and technical setup.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Thanks Ben — great summary. A few points from our side:

1) Stakeholders: please add Tom Willis (Infra) and myself for day-to-day. Priya (security) will review the security questionnaire and get back with classification.
2) Initial preference: we'd like to start with Hosted API for speed of setup, but we expect to evaluate Dedicated capacity during the PoC if the throughput can't be reliably handled by Hosted endpoints. If Dedicated proves necessary, we prefer a network-isolated pool (VPC peering) rather than full on-prem.
3) Success criteria: the latency and throughput targets look right. For cost we have internal thresholds (we can surface after week 1 once we see token usage).
4) Data handling: can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys for Hosted/Dedicated modes? Also need to know retention controls during the trial.

We can provision anonymized transcript samples by EOD Friday. Kickoff on Jun 17 works for our leads (Tom and Priya).

—Alex

Thanks Alex — great, that timeline works. A few clarifications and a concrete ask so we can get engineering prepped: 

1) KMS & retention: yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted API supports envelope encryption and short-term retention controls for trials; for strict KMS ownership we'd put you on a Dedicated pool or Private deployment. Marissa can share exact config details.

2) PoC scope: we'll run two parallel tracks unless you request Hosted-only:
  a) Hosted API sandbox (quickest): endpoints in us-west region, sample dataset ingest, functional validation, and load-run.
  b) Short Dedicated trial (2-week reserved pool): we can provision a small dedicated pool (4 A40-equivalent GPUs) for throughput testing and to validate scaling behavior. This is optional but recommended given your peak target.

3) Responsibilities:
  - Acme: provide anonymized transcripts and a named security contact (Priya is fine).
  - Redwood: provide trial endpoints, baseline load test scripts, and weekly sync.

4) Kickoff: propose Wed Jun 17 at 10:00am PT. Please confirm Tom, Priya, and Alex.

I've attached the PoC plan (detailed milestones) and updated success criteria. Marissa — can your team confirm the Dedicated pool sizing estimate and any infra prerequisites (VPC peering steps, IP allowlist)? Rishi — can you own weekly check-ins and any billing/commit questions if we flip to Dedicated?

Thanks,
Ben

Ben — quick technical notes for the thread so we have everything captured before kickoff: 

- Dedicated sizing: for 200 rps peak and p99 < 300ms we recommend starting with 4x A40-equivalent GPUs (NVIDIA A40 / similar) as a baseline for the dedicated pool. If your prompts average >1024 tokens we should bump to 6x.
- Data ingress: for Hosted sandbox we'll provide S3-compatible upload signed URLs; for Dedicated with VPC peering we can set up an S3 endpoint over the peered VPC or establish secure SFTP.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS requires a short onboarding window — please provide the KMS key ARN and the service account we'll use. We can lock down retention to 0 days for trial logs if the security team needs.
- Security questionnaire: I've attached the Acme-specific responses and highlighted a few items (audit logging, keys, and network controls) where we'll need Priya's input.

I'll prepare a short runbook for the Dedicated trial provisioning so infra knows what to expect (VPC CIDR, allowed IPs, peering steps). Ben — once Alex confirms Dedicated is desired, I'll start provisioning the reserved pool and pass along ETA (~48-72 hours).
